title: Associate skill translation & shadow handoff kit
content:
One-page kit for converting lateral/hire-with-transfer candidates and internal transfers into productive contributors quickly. This is intentionally light-weight and pragmatic — copyable checklist + short rubrics + shadow handoff schedule that hiring managers and new-hire buddies can use without extra meetings.

  Use cases covered:
  - internal transfer (within 30 days notice)
  - new external hire with strong adjacent domain skills (e.g., infra → serving-runtime)
  - contractor -> perm conversion

  Quick goals:
  1) validate core skill translation within first 14 days via paired tasks
  2) remove 3 operational blockers for independent work by day 30 (access, env, test harness)
  3) measurable impact / first small deliverable by day 60
  4) plan a 90-day growth loop with checkpoints and rubric-based calibration

  14-day rapid validation (shadow-focused)
  - Day 0 (pre-boarding): Manager submits HR-3421 and shares role context doc; buddy assigned; hardware & SSO ordered.
  - Day 1: 90m orientation with team + buddy: project map + immediate expectations (deliverable by day 30). Pair for 2 hrs on existing microtask (read + run tests).
  - Days 2–5: Shadow sessions (2 x 60m) with 2 different engineers. Focus: codebase tour, CI run, day-to-day debugging workflow. Buddy to capture 5 friction points.
  - End of week 1: short async update in #onboarding and link to short screen recording showing local dev run. Manager ticks off access checklist.
  - Days 8–14: paired microtask handoff — candidate takes first half of the microtask while buddy completes the second half; rotate ownership each day. Deliverable: PR to staging with tests.

  30-day operational checklist
  - access: ensure DB read-only, staging cluster creds, feature-flag console
  - environment: reproducible local dev script + docs updated for newcomer notes
  - tests: baseline integration test added by candidate
  - visibility: 1:1 cadence established (weekly recurring), first demo scheduled at week 4

  60-day impact & calibration
  - candidate delivers a scoped feature/bugfix end-to-end to staging
  - peer review participation: at least 3 reviews authored
  - rubric-based calibration (see rubric below) with hiring manager + buddy + people-ops
  - decision checkpoint: continue growth plan / targeted training / remediation

  90-day growth loop
  - identify 2 stretches aligned with team roadmap
  - assign mentor for cross-functional touchpoints (product/infra/security)
  - run a short eval on latency/cost/quality tradeoffs if role touches inference infra (example task provided below)

  Interviewer/hire-rubric (rapid version)
  - Problem framing (1–5): can articulate assumptions and tradeoffs
  - Tool fluency (1–5): can use repo, CI, and local profiling tools to reproduce an issue
  - Communication (1–5): writes clear PR descriptions and async updates
  - Ownership (1–5): proposes a plan with milestones and rollback strategy

  Rubric guidance (short):
  - 4–5 = ready to be ramped to independent work with buddy sign-off
  - 3 = needs targeted coachable gaps (pairing + 2 training sessions)
  - <=2 = extend shadowing and narrow-scope remediation plan

  Shadow handoff schedule (example 2-week calendar)
  - Week A: 50% observation, 50% paired tasks. Shadow engineers: EngA (day 2), EngB (day 4)
  - Week B: 25% observation, 75% ownership of microtask with buddy code reviews
  - Deliverable by end of week B: functioning PR + deployment runbook stub

  Microtask examples (pick one aligned to role):
  - Serving-runtime engineer: reproduce a regression on kv-cache eviction and add a regression test
  - Console engineer: add a simple per-route latency chart to an existing dashboard and write a short data note
  - SRE: write a short runbook to triage a GPU node OOM and document the mitigation steps

  Manager checklist (to be completed in 30 days)
  - Assign buddy and confirm 3 shadow sessions scheduled
  - Confirm hardware & SSO delivered
  - Share 30-day deliverable and acceptance criteria
  - Add new hire to team rota and oncall orientation if relevant
  - Book rubric calibration meeting at day 60

  People-ops procedural notes (quick):
  - expedite KMS/HSM requests for transfers touching customer keys (cc Security)
  - expense pre-approval for onboarding tools (VM images, paid training)
  - note to HR: use conversion template for contractor hires to keep start date continuity

  Quick templates (copy/paste)
  - 1:1 meeting agenda (week 1):
    * how did the first week feel? blockers?
    * quick demo of local run and tests
    * agree on microtask scope for week 2
  - Slack intro message for buddy to post in #onboarding:
    "Welcome @newhire! I’m your buddy. Today we’ll: run the local dev script, review the repo layout, and pair on a microtask. Ping me for anything."

  Open questions / unresolved
  - Should we require a minimum of 2 production-compatible PRs before removing buddy pairing for infra-adjacent transfers? Pros/cons documented but needs leadership decision.
  - Do we standardize the 14-day shadow checklist across all teams or allow team-level variants? (ops: propose a baseline + opt-out exceptions)

  Notes to self
  - capture anonymized examples of “fast successful transfer” and “slow ramp” cases for playbook appendix
  - check with Security on current KMS request SLA (used to be 14 days — reduce target)

  Appendix (short examples)
  - Example acceptance criteria for a 30-day microtask: plays on staging, passes CI, includes 1 regression test, README updated with dev steps, PR includes performance note.

  Bottom line: aim for speed without sacrificing signal. Shadowing + targeted paired tasks are the cheapest, fastest way to validate whether adjacent skills map to independent impact. This kit is opinionated — use the pieces that fit the team and log the divergences so we can iterate.
